chunks: The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Ruwayani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud.

He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said regarding the saying of God the Mighty and Majestic, 'Faces on that Day will be bright, looking toward their Lord' (75:22-23). He said: Meaning [their faces will be] illuminated, awaiting the reward of their Lord.

key_terms.نَاضِرَةٌ: nadhira — bright, radiant (not from n-z-r 'to see' but from n-d-r 'to be bright')
key_terms.نَاظِرَةٌ: nazhira — looking/waiting, interpreted here as 'awaiting' rather than 'gazing at'

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida interpret the Quran verse about faces looking toward their Lord?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida offers an interpretation of Quran 75:22-23 that is central to Shi'a theology. While some schools read 'looking at their Lord' (nazhira) as literal visual sight of God, Imam al-Rida interprets 'nadhira' (bright) as meaning illuminated/radiant, and 'nazhira' as meaning waiting for or anticipating God's reward. This reflects the Shi'a theological position (shared with Mu'tazili thought) that God cannot be seen with physical sight, and the verse describes spiritual illumination and eager expectation of divine reward on the Day of Resurrection.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: `Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Ruwayani narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Athim b. `Abdullah b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Zayd b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) narrated to me from Ibrahim b. Abi Mahmud.

He said: `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as) said, regarding the saying of Allah, "The faces on that day will be bright, looking at their Lord" (75:22-23). He said: Meaning, [their faces will be] illuminated, looking at the rewards of their Lord.
